## Result

Negative answer to Janssen's non-ACM gap-one line-configuration question, over every algebraically closed field: any nonempty reduced finite union of lines with alpha(I^(2))=alpha(I)+1 is coplanar or a complete pseudostar and hence ACM.

## Proof and review

- Complete characteristic-free adjoint/conductor proof in PUBLIC_TURN_2.md
- Separate full adversarial AI review: PASS_COMPLETE_ARBITRARY_CHARACTERISTIC_LINE_THEOREM
- 3,888 exact supplemental algebra controls, including characteristic 2 edge cases
- Two substantive recovered author turns; only the existing target QUEUE row changes to claimed_solved 2/5
- First-turn partial checkpoint preserved byte-for-byte and retained in commit ancestry; the earlier characteristic-zero scope correction remains visible

Classical inputs and existing pseudostar results are credited. The claim covers the source's line question, not arbitrary reduced curves. This is AI-assisted work and separate AI review, not human peer review or formal certification. Novelty and priority are not certified. No merge, release, DOI publication or external contact is requested.

## Final sweep publication coverage (21 October 2026 UTC)

The complete arbitrary-characteristic line theorem was independently rederived and passed separate new surface and configuration adversarial reviews. The retained exact controls reproduce the original 3,888 assertions and add 125,930 assertions, including all 59,535 configurations through four lines of PG(3,2). These finite controls supplement the universal proof.

An existing external paper by **Alper Ferudun**, published 10 October 2026 as [DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23284413](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23284413), already contains the exact full line theorem. Its archived PDF, source ZIP and verification report were downloaded and checked, the DOI resolves, and the result is recorded once in the tracker (Math Puzzles, row 175), with the external author credited. The external paper's ancillary claims are outside this coverage certification.

This PR's server creation is 2 October 2026. Historical repository visibility and first public disclosure are not adjudicated; the later overlap does not establish derivation or invalidate the earlier dated proof. The original draft and source are preserved, and no second Zenodo record was created for this result. The work is AI assisted and unrefereed; internal AI reviews are not formal independent human peer review.
